instruction: Identify all unique countries listed in the Country column of the open ods file, sort them alphabetically, and save them line by line in a text file called 'unique_countries.txt' on the Desktop using command line utilities.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting unique countries from the Country column (column 5) in the ODS file. Verified with Python: the file contains exactly 3 unique countries: France, Great Britain, and United States. Agent should convert ODS to CSV, then extract and sort unique values from the Country column using command line tools (e.g., cut, sort, uniq). Evaluator checks if all 3 countries are present in the output file.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements.
Getter logic is correct: Reads file at /home/user/Desktop/unique_countries.txt and returns content as string.
Metric correctly verifies presence of all expected countries: Checks if sorted(result_lines) == sorted(expected_items) to ensure all items present with no extras (line 22).
Metric correctly verifies uniqueness: Checks len(result_lines) != len(set(result_lines)) to detect duplicates (line 26-27).
Metric correctly verifies alphabetical sorting: Checks if result_lines != sorted(result_lines) to ensure proper ordering (line 30-31).
Metric correctly verifies one-per-line format: Splits by newline and strips whitespace (line 19).
Expected values are semantically correct: France, Great Britain, United States match the actual unique countries in the data file.
Postconfig is appropriate: Kills gnome-terminal-server to clean up terminal state after command execution.
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts file content → Metric validates all requirements → Returns 1.0 only if all checks pass.
